title: Circle Wrapped Bitcoin (cirBTC) — custodial FiatTokenV2_2 with permissioned mint
closed_reasons: cirBTC is Circle's FiatTokenV2_2 (USDC architecture) behind a FiatTokenProxy; mint() is onlyMinters and requires minterAllowance[msg.sender] >= amount
Minters/allowances are configured by the Circle MasterMinter contract; role changes (owner/masterMinter/pauser/blacklister) and rescueERC20 are role-gated; the proxy upgrade is admin-gated
No permissionless mint or release path exists (natively issued, not bridged from an escrow); burn only reduces the caller's own balance
Backing is custodial: 1:1 native BTC held by Circle International Bermuda Limited; redemption via KYC'd Circle Mint only

Attacker probes revert: mint -> 'FiatToken: caller is not a minter'; configureMinter -> 'caller is not the masterMinter'; updateMasterMinter -> 'Ownable: caller is not the owner'; pause -> 'not the pauser'; blacklist -> 'not the blacklister'; rescueERC20/updateOwner/upgradeTo -> revert

caveats: Point-in-time 2026-10-25; supply and roles can change
DefiLlama TVL differs from on-chain totalSupply (DefiLlama-side accounting/price); the on-chain supply is authoritative here
Proxy admin and owner are EOAs with no upgrade timelock — a centralisation (P) risk, not an unprivileged exploit
All work read-only; PoC executed only on an in-memory fork
one_liner: cirBTC is a custodial Circle FiatTokenV2_2 with a permissioned MasterMinter mint and role-gated admin: an external unprivileged attacker can extract $0; residual risk is Circle's EOA-held admin/upgrade keys (P) and KYC-gated redemption.
